description: Facts about a person that cannot be reissued, and a privilege field the caller filled in. The vocabulary for the first is short on purpose: measured across 28 production repositories these names appear three times, two of which are Passport the authentication library, so the bare word is not on the list. The two CWE-770 findings are a third rule on the same lines and all three are true: `users` is a module-level container keyed by an address the caller sent, so it gains an entry per address whatever the role written into it turns out to be -- which is why the route the privilege rule calls clean still reports here.

expected.note: a log is copied to more places than anyone tracks, and this cannot be reissued
where it goes after leaving this process is not this process's decision any more
the caller decides what this account may do; the same assignment from a constant below is silent
a different rule on the same line, and both are true: the role is the caller's AND the container gains an entry per address
the route the privilege rule calls clean, because what is written there is a constant; what it is written UNDER is still the caller's and still unbounded
